claims.claim: Action is exclusively dependent upon the constant presence of others and is the sole prerogative of man, unlike labor or work which can be imagined in isolation.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Action alone is the exclusive prerogative of man; neither a beast nor a god is capable of it, and only action is entirely dependent upon the constant presence of others.

claims.claim: The translation of Aristotle's zōon politikon as animal socialis or homo est naturaliter politicus, id est, socialis reflects a loss of the original Greek understanding of politics.
claims.supporting_excerpt: More than any elaborate theory, this unconscious substitution of the social for the political betrays the extent to which the original Greek understanding of politics had been lost.

definitions.definition: Human life in so far as it is actively engaged in doing something, always rooted in a world of men and of man-made things.

distinctions.distinction: Action and speech constitute the bios politikos and the realm of human affairs, from which everything merely necessary or useful is strictly excluded.

must_not_be_lost: The distinction between the Greek understanding of politics and the later Latin/modern social concept.
The unique status of action requiring the presence of others compared to labor and fabrication.
parsed.segment_function: The author introduces the chapter on the public and private realms by examining the distinction between human life as social versus political, discussing how activities like labor, work, and action relate to the company of others, and contrasting the ancient Greek political understanding with the later development of the social.
